name: Traverse
tagline: Labuan Bajo to Larantuka, west to east across the spine of Flores
description: The primary concept course: ten sections from the Komodo gateway to the Portuguese-Catholic east, crossing the island's volcanic spine repeatedly rather than following the paved Trans-Flores highway's single 670 km line. Single stage, self-supported, fixed route, with cultural checkpoints at villages that have agreed to host the race. All figures are concept sketches, drawn from docs/route-concept.md, pending the first scouting season.
notes: West to east because the prevailing dry-season wind is from the east-south-east and because the island's story reads that way, from Komodo and the Manggarai highlands to the Catholic-Portuguese east. Dry-season window late June to September; August is the safest weather bet and also the busiest month in Labuan Bajo. Variant B alternatives exist in data/segments.geojson for the same node pairs (Wae Rebo out-and-back, Boawae→Nangaroro direct, Lewotobi highway corridor) but are not part of this route's selected chain; they are candidates for scouts to evaluate against variant A.

name: Ultra
tagline: The Traverse plus the Manggarai Timur interior, the Bola coast loop, and the Inerie circuit
description: An extended variant for stakeholders and scouts weighing a longer, more remote course: it trades the direct Liang Bua→Reo→Pota corridor for the unscouted Ruteng→Borong→Elar→Pota interior of Manggarai Timur (+120-160 km per the route concept, using the upper end here), adds the Maumere→Bola→Watublapi south-coast loop before Egon (+50-70 km, upper end used), and swaps the Inerie shoulder traverse for a full circuit of the mountain (+40-60 km, upper end used). Every added kilometre here is even less scouted than the Traverse; treat this as a distance ceiling to test appetite for, not a proposal ready for a village agreement.
notes: Sketch total computed from the current concept-sketch segments falls close to but just under the low end of this target range (see the course-design report); the shortfall is reported honestly rather than closed by inventing distance beyond what docs/route-concept.md states. A fourth optional loop named in the concept (Riung→Mbay by the coast and the Bajawa plateau, +60-90 km) is not yet built as segments here because it revisits both the coast and the plateau rather than offering a simple point-to-point alternative; it remains a candidate for a future revision of this route.
